skill.name: docker-workflow
skill.description: Guides Docker containerization with multi-stage builds, Compose orchestration, image optimization, debugging, and production deployment practices.
skill.summary: Build, debug, optimize, and harden Docker images and multi-service Compose environments.
skill.author: bossjones

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Markdown fences, ignore rules, localhost checks, and Docker template syntax. Confirmed risks include embedded example secrets, an executable Docker helper, and its public connectivity probe. Semantic review found insecure service defaults, secret disclosure, destructive cleanup, and unpinned images; no prompt injection was found.

remediation.issue: Predictable credentials are embedded in Compose service definitions.
remediation.suggestion: Replace defaults with required environment variables or Docker secrets, and fail startup when values are missing.

remediation.issue: Elasticsearch disables authentication while publishing its HTTP port.
remediation.suggestion: Enable Elasticsearch security and bind the port to localhost or an authenticated private network.

remediation.issue: The helper prints container environment values without redaction.
remediation.suggestion: Show variable names by default and require explicit confirmation before displaying redacted values.

remediation.issue: Cleanup force-prunes Docker volumes and other resources.
remediation.suggestion: Add a confirmation prompt, support a dry run, and exclude volumes unless the user requests them.

remediation.issue: The connectivity test always contacts a public IP address.
remediation.suggestion: Make the target configurable and default to an operator-approved internal endpoint.

remediation.issue: Several Compose services use mutable latest tags.
remediation.suggestion: Pin reviewed versions or image digests and document a controlled update process.

semantic_findings.title: Hardcoded Service Credentials in Reusable Compose Template
semantic_findings.description: The Compose template defines predictable PostgreSQL, Redis, RabbitMQ, Grafana, and pgAdmin credentials. Copying these defaults can expose data and administrative interfaces.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The credentials are directly visible in active service definitions. Several associated interfaces are published to host ports.

semantic_findings.title: Elasticsearch Authentication Disabled on Published Port
semantic_findings.description: The Compose template disables Elasticsearch security while publishing port 9200. A non-local deployment could expose indexed data without authentication.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The active service sets xpack.security.enabled=false and publishes 9200. Docker binds published ports broadly unless deployment settings restrict them.

semantic_findings.title: Container Environment Disclosure Helper
semantic_findings.description: The env command prints every environment variable from a running container. Secrets can enter terminal history, recordings, or support logs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The helper directly runs env and sorts the unredacted output. No secret-name filtering or confirmation is present.

semantic_findings.title: Forced Cleanup Can Delete Persistent Docker Data
semantic_findings.description: The cleanup command force-prunes containers, images, volumes, and networks without confirmation. Unused volumes can still contain valuable application data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The function invokes four prune commands with forced flags. The command handler runs the function without an additional confirmation step.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Container Images in Compose Template
semantic_findings.description: Several services use latest image tags. Future pulls can introduce unreviewed changes or compromised upstream releases.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Four active services explicitly use latest tags. The template provides no digest pinning or update verification workflow.

content.user_title: Build Reliable Docker Workflows With AI
content.value_statement: Docker projects often need consistent builds, service orchestration, debugging, and production safeguards. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through practical container workflows.
actual_capabilities: Drafts .dockerignore rules that reduce build context and exclude common secrets.
Creates multi-stage Dockerfile guidance for Node.js, Python, Go, Java, and Rust.
Designs Docker Compose stacks with services, networks, volumes, dependencies, and health checks.
Provides commands and a helper script for logs, inspection, shells, ports, processes, and health checks.
Analyzes image layers and recommends caching, smaller bases, BuildKit, and runtime hardening.
Explains deployment patterns using non-root users, pinned images, health checks, and vulnerability scanning.
limitations: The skill does not validate generated configurations against a live Docker daemon.
Examples require project-specific paths, commands, ports, image versions, and package files.
The Compose template contains development credentials that must be replaced before shared or production use.
The helper can expose environment values or delete unused Docker resources when explicitly run.

use_cases.title: Containerize a New Application
use_cases.description: Create a multi-stage Dockerfile, .dockerignore rules, and a local Compose stack for an existing project.

use_cases.title: Optimize Container Builds
use_cases.description: Review layers, dependency caching, base images, build contexts, and runtime users to reduce size and improve reliability.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Container Failures
use_cases.description: Investigate logs, health checks, ports, mounts, processes, resources, and service networking with a repeatable workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Create My First Dockerfile
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my project structure and draft a multi-stage Dockerfile. Explain each stage and identify every project-specific value I must provide.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Compose Environment
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Docker Compose environment for my application, database, cache, and worker. Include networks, volumes, dependencies, and health checks.

prompt_templates.title: Debug a Failing Container
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this container failure using logs, health status, ports, mounts, processes, and networking. Prioritize checks and explain each conclusion.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these Dockerfile and Compose files. Review secrets, privileges, image pinning, exposed services, health checks, build size, and destructive operations.

output_examples.input: A Node.js API needs a smaller production image and reliable startup checks.
output_examples.output: A staged build plan covering dependency caching, runtime-only files, a non-root user, health checks, and image size verification.

output_examples.input: A local stack needs an API, PostgreSQL, Redis, and a background worker.
output_examples.output: A service design with isolated networks, named volumes, health-based dependencies, required secrets, and limited host port exposure.

output_examples.input: A container starts but remains unhealthy and cannot reach its database.
output_examples.output: A prioritized checklist for health output, logs, service DNS, network membership, database readiness, credentials, and port configuration.

best_practices: Replace all example credentials and restrict published service ports before deployment.
Review helper operations before running them on shared hosts or systems with persistent volumes.
Pin image versions, run as non-root, define health checks, and scan images before release.
anti_patterns: Do not copy development passwords or disabled authentication settings into shared environments.
Do not print container environment values into support tickets, recordings, or shared logs.
Do not force-prune Docker volumes without confirming ownership, backups, and retention requirements.

faq.question: Does this skill run Docker commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and scripts. Docker commands run only when a user or agent explicitly executes them.

faq.question: Which application languages are covered?
faq.answer: The included multi-stage examples cover Node.js, Python, Go, Java, and Rust.

faq.question: Does it support Docker Compose?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers services, networks, volumes, dependencies, health checks, overrides, monitoring, queues, and caches.

faq.question: Can I use the examples in production?
faq.answer: Only after review. Replace credentials, enable authentication, restrict ports, pin images, and adapt every project-specific value.

faq.question: What can the helper script inspect?
faq.answer: It can inspect health, logs, resources, networks, ports, environment values, processes, images, and mounted volumes.

faq.question: What destructive operations are included?
faq.answer: The cleanup command force-prunes stopped containers, dangling images, unused volumes, and unused networks.
